title: telemetry-contract-for-ml-inference-features-2027
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose
This page defines the telemetry contract for ML inference features across Redwood Inference: the required metric names, log schema, trace/span conventions, sampling rules, privacy redaction, ingestion budgets, and CI checks that instrumenters must follow. It covers backend serving runtimes, edge proxies, private deployment sidecars, and SDK clients.

Scope and goals
- Scope: server-side inference stacks (hosted, dedicated, private) and first-party SDKs. Does NOT include end-user application telemetry (app-level business events), except where necessary for debug correlation (see Correlation Keys).
- Goals: consistent dimensions for cost attribution, fast root-cause analysis, compact signals to control telemetry cost, and forward-compatible schema evolution.

High-level contract summary
1) Every inference request must emit: a minimal set of metrics, a request-scoped trace, and a structured request/response log event at INFO on request completion (success or failure).
2) Metric names and labels must follow the naming conventions below. Labels should be sparse and low-cardinality.
3) Sampling: full traces and logs in staging; sampling applied in prod per-tenant as defined in the Telemetry Budget table. Metrics are always emitted.
4) PII: prompts and user text MUST be redacted or hashed before being written to logs/attributes. See Privacy section.

Naming and schema conventions (summary table)
- Metric namespace: redwood.inference.<area>.<signal>
  - Examples: redwood.inference.runtime.latency_p50_ms, redwood.inference.request.count
- Metric types: counters (suffix _total), gauges, histograms (suffix _bucket or explicit _hist).
- Labels: service, model_id, model_variant, deployment_tier, region, request_class, route, tenant_id (hashed). Keep label cardinality limited to < 1k unique values per label in production.

Required metrics (prometheus-style names suggested)
- redwood_inference_request_total (counter) labels: service, model_id, request_class, deployment_tier, region
- redwood_inference_error_total (counter) labels: service, model_id, error_type, deployment_tier, region
- redwood_inference_latency_ms_bucket (histogram) labels: service, model_id, deployment_tier, region
- redwood_inference_kv_cache_hit_total (counter) labels: service, model_id, cache_tier
- redwood_inference_token_cost_sum (counter) labels: service, model_id, billing_tier

Metric label guidance
- model_id: use the model capability manifest id (short form), not full path. Example: ggml-v1-small.
- model_variant: allowed for rollout / A/B testing, but avoid including commit SHAs.
- request_class: one of {sync, streaming, async-batch, batch-job, embed}. Use this to drive routing and SLA mapping.

Structured log event schema (single JSON object per request completion)
- timestamp: RFC3339
- request_id: UUID v4 (top-level correlation key)
- trace_id: hex (if available)
- service: string (e.g., inference-router)
- endpoint: string (API route or internal RPC name)
- model_id: string
- model_variant: string
- tenant_id_hash: sha256 base64 (do not store raw tenant ids)
- request_class: enum
- seq_len_in: integer
- seq_len_out: integer
- tokens_consumed: integer
- latency_ms: integer
- status: {ok, client_error, server_error, throttled}
- error_code: string (empty when status==ok)
- prompt_hash: sha256 hex (only hashed prompts are allowed in logs)
- sample_rate: decimal (fraction used for traces/logs)
- extra_labels: map[string]string (freeform but must be limited; CI check enforces max 4 keys)

Example log (single-line JSON)
{"timestamp":"2027-02-18T12:15:02Z","request_id":"9f8a2e3c-...","trace_id":"ab1f...","service":"inference-worker","endpoint":"/v1/generate","model_id":"llama-13b-q4","model_variant":"v2-canary","tenant_id_hash":"3f2b...","request_class":"sync","seq_len_in":52,"seq_len_out":128,"tokens_consumed":180,"latency_ms":312,"status":"ok","error_code":"","prompt_hash":"5b3a...","sample_rate":"0.02","extra_labels":{"route":"assistant-default"}}

Trace/span conventions
- Use OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where applicable. Root span name: inference.request.<request_class>. Child spans: authorization, routing, model.invoke, kv.cache.lookup, postprocess.
- Each span must include: span.kind, model_id, model_variant, request_id, and tenant_id_hash.
- model.invoke should report token_count_in/out and bytes_sent/received as attributes.

Sampling strategy and telemetry budget
- Staging: sample_rate = 1.0 (capture everything).
- Production: default sample_rate = 0.02 (2%) for traces and detailed logs. The frontend router may apply dynamic sampling per tenant to respect budgets below.
- Telemetry budget table (per-tenant default limits):
  - max_trace_events_per_minute: 120
  - max_log_events_per_minute: 600
  - metric_ingestion_limit: 5000 metric series (soft limit; alert owners when > 4000)
- Any service expecting to exceed these defaults for a tenant must file a telemetry budget exception with SRE and product.

Privacy and redaction rules
1) Never log raw prompt text, user messages, or uploads. Record only prompt_hash and derived metadata (seq_len, tokens_consumed, prompt_class).
2) If a user explicitly requests debug logs that include input text (for support), require an explicit temporary permission token and store logs in a restricted retention bucket with confidentiality=restricted.
3) Keys/IDs that identify customers must be hashed before emission (tenant_id_hash).

Cost-control and ingestion enforcement
- Instrumentation owners must:
  - Ensure metrics are exported using low-cardinality labels.
  - Avoid freeform keys in extra_labels beyond 4 keys.
  - Prefer counters and histograms over high-cardinality gauges.
- The telemetry ingestion pipeline enforces soft quotas and will mark tenants for quota review if they exceed limits for 3 consecutive days. Runbook: See /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/telemetry-quota-escalation (link).

Alerting & SLOs for telemetry health
- Telemetry SLO: 99.9% of request-level metrics emitted within 30s of completion for production traffic.
- Default alerts to configure:
  - metric_emission_latency > 30s for >5m (sev-2)
  - unusual_metric_cardinality_growth: metric series count delta > 1k in 10m (sev-2)
  - dropped_trace_rate > 5% in 30m (sev-1)

Instrumentation checklist (pre-merge)
1) Add metric definitions to metrics catalog (YAML entry).
2) Add log schema example to service README.
3) Add trace/span assertions to unit/integration tests (use test fixture that verifies attribute names and types).
4) Run telemetry-lint CI step (see enforcement below).

CI enforcement: telemetry-lint
- telemetry-lint runs as part of the service repo CI and performs:
  - Schema validation of log JSON examples (max keys, required fields).
  - Label-cardinality heuristics (warn if a label value comes from unbounded input).
  - Prometheus metric name/style checks.
  - Fails if prompt sample appears in committed example logs.

Versioning and schema evolution
- Telemetry schema changes must be additive. Breaking changes require:
  1) ADR describing rationale and migration plan (see Decision Record section below).
  2) 30-day deprecation window with warnings in platform logs and dashboards.
  3) Dual-writes for 30 days where feasible.
- Use a top-level schema_version attribute in logs and traces to simplify migration: schema_version: "1.0".

Enforcement and rollout
- New instrumentation is staged to staging with full capture. After 7 days of clean telemetry and CI passes, enable in a 1% prod rollout, verify ingestion cost and metric stability for 72h, then ramp to target sampling.
- Owners must tag instrumentation PRs with the label telemetry:instrumentation to trigger SRE review.

Ownership and onboarding
- Owner responsibilities: maintain metric definitions, react to alerts, own data retention exemptions.
- Onboarding docs: Add a short guide in each service repo README pointing to this page and providing the sample log and sample metrics.

Decision record summary (why this contract)
- Decision: Adopt a constrained, low-cardinality telemetry contract for inference that prioritizes metric availability and correlation while limiting ingestion costs and PII risk.
- Alternatives considered: allow freeform logs and labels (rejected due to ingestion explosion), keep tracing fully un-sampled (rejected on cost), record raw prompts (rejected on privacy).
- Consequences: Developers must adapt to hashed/pseudonymized correlation keys and accept sampling for traces/logs in prod. There is a modest operational burden to maintain telemetry budgets and CI checks but significant win in predictable observability costs and privacy posture.

Related artifacts and links
- Telemetry budget playbook: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/telemetry-budget-enrichment-playbook-2026
- Telemetry CI implementation: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/telemetry-lint-service
- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/telemetry-quota-escalation

Appendix: quick-check list for reviewers
- Required metrics present and named correctly? (yes/no)
- Log JSON example included and contains prompt_hash (not raw prompt)? (yes/no)
- Prometheus label cardinality reviewed? (yes/no)
- CI telemetry-lint green? (yes/no)
- PII/Privacy review completed? (yes/no)

Contact and stewardship
Telemetry and observability stewardship: Observability Guild -> obs-guild@redwood.example.com. For budget exceptions contact: telemetry-budget@redwood.example.com.
